title: Density-aware edge and tactile token update for buttons, tables, and charts
creator: Ava Patel
description: Audit and introduce a set of density-aware 'edge' and 'tactile-weight' tokens to improve perceived affordance and legibility for compact UI. This work covers: (1) token definitions and naming conventions for edge strokes and tactile weight (button press visual weight), (2) responsive radius deltas tied to density tokens, (3) compact-table row divider strategies (stroke vs inset shadow), and (4) a micro-elevation ramp for charts and data-overlays that preserves contrast at small sizes. Deliverables are spec files, migration guidelines, Figma component updates, and a partner PR for the token transform script. Goal: reduce visual clutter in dense views while preserving accessible contrast and consistent hit affordances across device sizes.
acceptance_criteria: New token set documented in design tokens spec page with clear token names and example usage
Figma component library updated — buttons/tables/charts reflect density tokens for default and compact modes
Contrast audit passes WCAG AA for primary/secondary button text and table row separators at compact density
Migration script (infra/token-transform) PR submitted and passes CI; consumers can opt-in to token deltas
Console and runtime perf notes recorded: shadow implementation choices evaluated for GPU compositing vs raster cost
migration_plan: 1) Publish token spec and rubric for deprecation of legacy stroke tokens. 2) Ship design token package v3.2 with opt-in 'density' flag. 3) Run token-transform script to generate delta-map for consumers; open PRs in top 10 consumers. 4) Two-week canary on production console with telemetry to measure layout regressions. 5) Full rollout after signoff from PM and Core UX.
notes: Trade-offs: using CSS box-shadow for micro-elevation is simpler but can be heavier on rasterization in older Chromium; SVG filters are expensive and unacceptable for streaming charts. We recommend 1-layer box-shadow + 1px subtle inset stroke for compact tables.
Naming convention: edge.* tokens for strokes (edge.x-weak | edge.x-regular | edge.x-strong); tactile.* tokens for perceived press weight (tactile.light | tactile.medium | tactile.firm).

We evaluated three approaches for compact-radius: proportional delta (radius * 0.6), absolute clamp (min 2px), and perceptual stepping; perceptual stepping chosen to avoid fractional radii in 1x assets.
Accessibility: lowered stroke opacity can break contrast at small sizes — we propose using neutral-600 at 8% for separators, with fallback neutral-700 at 12% for high-contrast mode.
